the lifetimes of postsynaptic receptor channel activations are governed by desensitization and that structural differences within extracellular and trans-membrane domains of homomultimeric Cys-loop receptors account for the contrasting properties of the two receptors.

the lifetimes of agonist-activated postsynaptic nicotinic and 5-hydroxytryptamine receptors are governed by the rate of desensitizing receptor channels, which in turn is determined by the structure of the interface between the extracellular and the transmembrane domains.

the lifetimes of postsynaptic receptor ion channels are determined by the rate of desensitizing and that the rate of desenstization is determined by the structure of the interface between the extracellular and the transmembrane domain of the receptor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural basis of functional differences in homomeric Cys-loop receptors, with a particular focus on α7 and 3-HT3A nicotinic and 5-HT receptors, respectively.
how the structural properties of Cys-loop receptors contribute to their function.
the mechanisms that control the lifetimes of postsynaptic ion channels.

the structural differences in the interface of the α7 and 3HT3A receptors account mainly for the differences in the open-channel lifetime and the onset of the desensitization of these two receptors.
the interface of the two domains, extracellular and trans-membrane, is the major factor in the differences in the open-channel lifetime and desensitization of the two Cys-loop receptors.
the interface between the extracellular and the transmembrane domains is a major determinant of the functional properties of homomeric receptors.

desensitizing ligand-gated ion channels are not just a mechanism of termination, but rather a major determinant of the lifetime of activated channels.
